I just recently picked up a Hohm Wrecker G2 and I've been using my Triton 2 tank with SS coils. It's pretty dang sweet, but I've been shopping around for a new tank and saw the Cleito from Aspire. Well the Hohm Wrecker just got a firmware updated that does Kanthal but Aspire says the coil is "claptonized kanthal". I have no clue what that is or if it will even work well. Has anyone been using a similar setup or could anyone recommend a great subohm tank for temp control?

Tl;dr: Whats a great subohm tank for temp control?

In general, the likelihood that the Hohm Wrecker folks have figured out temperature control with Kanthal is highly unlikely. It's much more likely that it has a function similar to Heat Protection that Dicodes use, and that Asolo have for Kanthal on their mods. Pragmatically, it's very similar to TC, but thre is no way to know what the temperature actually is.

As a general piece of advice: anything that is properly calibrated and is set to over 420 degrees Fahrenheit and does not burn your cotton does not have good TC performance. It could be the chip, it could be the kind of wire used inside the mod, or it could be the atomizer, but that's what's happening. If you take a look at Twisted's reviews, almost all of his TC mods are set to over 500 degrees on cotton, and clearly are not doing that.

The Claptonized Kanthal just means it's a Clapton coil, which looks like this. It's a thicker gauge of Kanthal with a thinner gauge wrapped all the way around it. Heat protection modes will work fine since they're not dependent on changes in resistance (how TC works in...all mods), but rather based on timing.

I don't really venture much into Sub Ohm tank territory, but I do use TC day in and day out with RBAs. I've used some of the Ni200 and Ti Innokin iSub coils, and they work really well, but are not without their pros and cons like anything else.

Look for coils that are built into the 510 connection (excluding the Altus, that atty is hot garbage). The fewer connection points between the coil and the mod, the better the resistance reading and more precise the temperature control will be.

I got my Crown to run in temp mode on a couple of my mods with the included Ni coilhead. I get the idea behind it, but it's not my cup o vape. If it works for others, by all means and enjoy your vape - I'll stick to wattage mode, personally.
